title: Adam's du'a
hook: our Lord, we have wronged ourselves (7:23)

segments.voice: Yesterday, jannah, and your line: their greeting is peace. Did three people get a real salam? The great themes are done. Now, eight days with the prophets' own prayers, starting where the garden story starts. Day six hundred eighty-eight.

Think of the last time you were caught. A broken dish, a missed deadline, words you wished you hadn't said. Notice what came out first. Usually it's one of two things. It wasn't my fault. Or, it was mine. In the Qur'an's garden story, two creatures get it wrong, and each one says one of those two sentences. The first prayer a human being ever prays in the Qur'an is the second one.

Surah al-A'raf tells it. Iblis is commanded to bow to Adam and refuses. His reason: I am better than him; You made me from fire and him from clay. Later, sent out, he says: because You have led me astray. Blame upward, blame outward. Then Adam and his wife eat from the tree they'd been told to leave alone. And in verse twenty-three, in Pickthall's translation: "They said: Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If Thou forgive us not and have not mercy on us, surely we are of the lost!" Notice three things. First, they. Both of them pray it together; the Qur'an doesn't put the blame on her. Second, ourselves. Not the serpent, not the tree, not each other. The wrong is named as damage done to their own souls. Third, the request is only forgiveness and mercy, with nothing bargained. Al-Baqarah says Adam received words from his Lord, and Allah turned to him in forgiveness. Many commentators say those words were this very prayer: Allah taught Adam how to come back, and then accepted it. In Islamic teaching, that forgiveness closed the matter. The Qur'an says no soul carries another's burden, so Adam's children are each born free of his slip. The garden story ends, in the Qur'an, not with a curse but with a returned prayer. Du'a, the word for this kind of personal prayer, comes from a root meaning to call. Adam's is the first call, and it's three words long at its heart: rabbana zalamna anfusana.

The practice: say it once. Sit quietly, and let one recent wrong of yours come to mind. Small is fine. Notice the excuse that usually comes with it, and set the excuse down beside you. Now, if you pray, say Adam's words once, slowly: rabbana zalamna anfusana, our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If you don't pray, say the plain version to yourself: that was mine. Then breathe, and let the rest of the sit be quiet. The bell holds the time.
Adam's du'a. Rabbana zalamna anfusana: our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. The first human prayer, taught by Allah and accepted. Today's word.
Your line: we wronged ourselves. Today, the next time something goes wrong that was partly yours, say so first, before any explanation. Day six hundred eighty-eight.

howItsDone: Many Muslims memorize Adam's du'a (7:23) and say it when seeking forgiveness, often in the prostration or after the prayer.

fork.setup: you're Adam. you and your wife have eaten from the tree. what do you say?
options: our Lord, we have wronged ourselves.
Iblis tricked us; it was him.
fork.reveal: they own it together, ask only for forgiveness and mercy, and Allah turns to them (7:23; 2:37).

original.note: Arabic, 7:23: our Lord, we have wronged ourselves.

trapdoor: what you thought: Adam's story is about a fall.
what it means: it ends with a prayer: we have wronged ourselves; forgive us, and Allah turns to them.
what a scholar hears: many commentators read the words of 2:37 as 7:23 itself; Iblis blames, Adam owns, and Islamic teaching holds no inherited sin.
